newsitem.title: USA: N.J. sets votes on port dredging, tank remediation.
newsitem.headline: N.J. sets votes on port dredging, tank remediation.

text.p: The New Jersey Legislature plans to vote Monday on implementing a $300 million bond-financed plan for port dredging approved by voters in November, legislative leaders said Friday.

The bill for dredging the ports in New York/New Jersey Harbor will be considered by both houses of the Legislature Monday. It would set up the administrative mechanism for deciding how to prioritize the various components of the project.

Senate President Donald DiFrancesco, who sponsored the 1996 referendum and the implementation legislation, said the measure "protects $20 billion in economic activity and 180,000 jobs that depend on an active shipping industry."

In addition to the port bill, the state Senate said Friday it would vote Monday on legislation to implement a second bond act approved by voters in November. That plan would finance hazardous waste site cleanup and underground storage tank remediation.
